subject: chemistry
title: Group 0: Noble Gases
welcome_lead: Stable, sparkling and seriously unreactive: the noble family of gases.
meta_desc: Meet the noble gases in this KS3 chemistry adventure on group 0 of the periodic table.
final_note: You can now explain why noble gases are so chemically chilled.

concepts.def: Noble gases: helium, neon, argon, krypton, xenon, radon.
Very unreactive gas with a full outer electron shell.
Lighter than air; used to fill balloons.
Used in some light bulbs to stop the filament burning.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Group 0 (sometimes Group 8) sits on the far right of the table. The noble gases are all colourless gases at room temperature.

Helium, neon, argon and friends.

Noble gases have a full outer electron shell. They don't need to gain, lose or share electrons, so they hardly ever react.

They are stable just as they are.

Because they don't react, noble gases are very useful:

Helium fills airships and balloons; neon glows in signs; argon protects metal welding and light bulb filaments.
